reviewer.role: independent bounded CODE-PROOF state, retained-I/O and installer reviewer

verdict: R5 closes the two R4 semantic findings and corrects the observed installer/budget mismatch. Its state matrix explicitly separates normalized and raw modes, rejects forbidden empty families, binds every reuse to the command's initial complete snapshot and disallows late identical-file adoption. The selected no-replace hard-link primitive correctly charges temporary and final logical names simultaneously with C + 2*N. No remaining state or budget contradiction was found. The candidate is not an implementation freeze: the concrete retained-session API, all-exits race behavior, closed public schemas/error mapping/resource hashes and independent adversarial evidence remain required gates.
scope: Read-only review of CODE-PROOF-STATE-AND-INSTALL-R5 against immutable CODE-PROOF-DESIGN-R2, CODE-PROOF-CLOSURE-R3, CODE-PROOF-IDENTITY-LAYOUT-R4, its corrected review metadata, the architect public-layout follow-up and the actual legacy staging installer. No source, schema, test, Git, provider, network, connector, Vault, implementation or public-wire mutation.

findings.evidence: R5 lines 12-46 captures a complete initial namespace snapshot before classification, makes request-only and both normalized states explicit, permits raw bodies only after a retained bundle, and states that every other combination—including empty forbidden files/directories—refuses. Lines 29-38 preserve the universal normalized-mode prohibition and the rule that derived families require a complete raw observation.
findings.risk_closed: Status and repair can no longer reinterpret an empty bundle/objects/configs/handoffs family as pending normalized data or delete it as an implicit repair.
findings.residual: The exact public status/refusal wording and error envelope remain a later wire-freeze dependency.

findings.evidence: R5 lines 48-55 require initial-snapshot presence, retained descriptor, named identity, exact type/mode/link count and exact bytes for every reusable request, intent, bundle, body, observation and derived file. A target first seen after captured absence is a lineage refusal even when bytes match; files created by the current command are tracked separately as authorized installations.
findings.risk_closed: A late identical config/body/metadata insertion cannot be adopted into the batch lineage as if it had been present initially.
findings.residual: The retained session must carry the per-slot/family origin and authorized-install state through retries; the required representation is an implementation-freeze dependency.

findings.evidence: R5 lines 65-75 explicitly records that legacy staging._atomic_install uses a sibling temp, no-replace hard-link and temp unlink rather than same-inode rename, and selects a private CODE installer using retained descriptors, os.link(follow_symlinks=False), no replacement and an open source descriptor through publication/cleanup.
findings.actual_legacy_observation: staging.py lines 731-743 create/write/fsync/fstat then close the temp descriptor before link; lines 751-781 hard-link and adopt an identical existing target on EEXIST; lines 690-694 and 805-808 use _unlink_at, which silently swallows unlink errors.
findings.risk_closed: R4's unverified same-inode rename premise and reuse-on-late-EEXIST behavior are not carried into the new CODE installer.
findings.residual: The selected primitive still needs a concrete retained-session implementation and race-bound review; legacy staging helpers remain unchanged.

findings.evidence: R5 lines 77-110 scopes the 134217728-byte cap to logical files under one output namespace, counts temporary and final names separately, charges observed regular-file stat sizes before reading even for pending/orphan/refused entries, rejects unsafe/unknown entries, and requires C + 2*N before an absent-target temp is created. Lines 89-94 define the 0/N/2*N/N transient phases and the sole permitted link-count-two inode.
findings.risk_closed: A hard-link publication cannot be justified by the prior current+N budget; the extra live logical name is explicitly accounted for.
findings.residual: The API must update C after each serialized install, keep one temp at a time, and prove exact boundary behavior for zero-byte and maximum-size payloads.

findings.evidence: R5 lines 114-130 require pre-install directory/input/resource revalidation, target-absence verification, complete-set checks, descriptor identity, exact bytes/mode/link count, no-replace publication, owned-temp cleanup, final directory fsync and all-exits lineage validation. Lines 140-145 explicitly refuse any claim that stat/unlink is an atomic compare-and-unlink and give persistent lineage failure precedence.
findings.risk_closed: The design does not silently treat retained descriptors as a lock against unrelated writers or claim a race-free compare-and-unlink operation.
findings.residual: Concrete checkpoint ordering, failure evidence and public result mapping are deliberately deferred to the retained-session API freeze.

findings.evidence: R5 lines 132-145 correctly require surfaced cleanup failures, refusal without unlinking a replaced temp, and no unconditional rollback of a possibly replaced final. However, it does not itself define the exact retained-session state/result when the source name is replaced between named-edge validation and os.link, when link succeeds but post-link identity verification fails, or when final directory fsync fails after temp cleanup.
findings.risk: A future implementation could leave a verified prefix, an unknown foreign sibling, or a mismatched final with inconsistent status/error evidence unless the all-exits API defines each checkpoint and precedence precisely.
findings.required_closure: Freeze the retained session's checkpoint/result matrix for target appearance, temp replacement/missing/unsafe, link-count change, link/fsync/unlink failures and post-link final identity mismatch; bind adversarial tests to that matrix.

findings.evidence: R5 lines 1-8, 101-102 and 152-154 expressly leave the six closed envelope data schemas, exact retained-session API, public error mapping, profile/resource hashes and independent review as separate requirements.
findings.risk: The state and installer rules cannot yet be implemented or externally accepted against a closed public contract.
findings.required_closure: Freeze all six envelope data schemas and bounds, materialized profile/resource byte hashes, error codes/details distinguishing budget from lineage, retained-session API and exact allowed implementation/test paths before dispatch.

findings.evidence: R5 lines 147-154 lists target-appearance, temporary replacement, link-count, short/zero-write, fsync/link/unlink, directory replacement, unknown sibling, initial parse/size and cleanup failures, plus exact C+2*N boundary/transient phases, as required independent review vectors.
findings.risk: The candidate states the required tests but contains no executed implementation or evidence because no retained CODE API has been frozen or handed off.
findings.required_closure: After exact stopped candidate handoff, run the listed vectors against the concrete private installer and unchanged legacy helpers; preserve candidate hashes and independent review output.
